nodes.title: Windows: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Windows. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What Windows tool allows you to check and repair disk errors?
flashcards.back: CHKDSK (Check Disk) scans the file system for errors and bad sectors. Run 'chkdsk /f' to fix errors or 'chkdsk /r' to find and recover bad sectors.

flashcards.front: Which Windows command shows current IP configuration?
flashcards.back: 'ipconfig' shows IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway. 'ipconfig /all' shows all details including MAC address and DNS servers.

flashcards.front: Which Windows tool lets you manage startup programs?
flashcards.back: In Windows 10/11, the Startup tab in Task Manager shows and manages startup programs. 'msconfig' (System Configuration) also manages startup items and is useful for troubleshooting.

flashcards.front: Which file system is used by default on modern Windows installations?
flashcards.back: NTFS (New Technology File System) is the default for Windows installations. It supports large files, permissions, encryption (EFS), compression, and journaling. FAT32 is used for USB drives.

nodes.title: Hardware: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Hardware. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is the speed of USB 3.0?
flashcards.back: USB 3.0 (USB 3.2 Gen 1) operates at 5 Gbps. USB 2.0 = 480 Mbps, USB 3.1 Gen 2 = 10 Gbps, USB4 = up to 40 Gbps.

flashcards.front: Which component stores the BIOS/UEFI firmware and system settings when power is ?
flashcards.back: CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor) RAM stores BIOS settings and is powered by a small coin-cell battery (CR2032) on the motherboard when main power is off.

flashcards.front: Which display connector carries both audio and video signals digitally?
flashcards.back: HDMI carries both digital video and audio in a single cable. VGA is analog video only. DVI carries digital/analog video but no audio. DisplayPort also carries audio and video.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of thermal paste on a CPU?
flashcards.back: CPU surfaces aren't perfectly flat. Thermal compound fills micro-gaps between the CPU IHS and heatsink, dramatically improving heat transfer from processor to cooler.

pairs.stem: What is the purpose of thermal paste on a CPU?
pairs.option: Fills microscopic gaps between the CPU and heatsink to improve thermal conductivity

nodes.title: Storage: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Storage. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What does RAID 1 provide?
flashcards.back: RAID 1 mirrors data across two drives. If one fails, the other has an identical copy. No performance gain for writes; read performance can improve. Usable space = 50% of total.

flashcards.front: What is 'imaging' a drive in IT support?
flashcards.back: Drive imaging (tools: Clonezilla, Macrium Reflect, Acronis) captures an exact bit-for-bit copy. Used for: PC deployment (image many PCs from one master), disaster recovery, forensic evidence collection.

flashcards.front: What does S.M.A.R.T. technology do for hard drives?
flashcards.back: SMART monitors parameters like reallocated sectors, spin-up time, error rates, power-on hours, and temperature. Tools like CrystalDiskInfo read SMART data. SMART Caution/Fail warnings = imminent failure — back up immediately. and Reporting Technology — continuously monitors drive health indicators and predicts failure to enable proactive replacement

flashcards.front: What is SMART monitoring for hard drives?
flashcards.back: SMART attributes are checked via tools like CrystalDiskInfo, HD Sentinel. Critical attributes: Reallocated Sector Count (bad sectors remapped), Uncorrectable Sector Errors, Spin Retry Count. Any 'CAUTION' or 'BAD' status = replace immediately.

pairs.stem: What does RAID 1 provide?
pairs.option: Mirroring — exact copy of data on two drives for redundancy

pairs.stem: What does S.M.A.R.T. technology do for hard drives?
What is the difference between MBR and GPT disk partitioning?
What is 'imaging' a drive in IT support?
pairs.option: Creating a sector-by-sector exact copy of an entire drive — including OS, partitions, and data — for backup, cloning, or forensics

pairs.stem: What is the purpose of disk defragmentation and should you defrag an SSD?
pairs.option: HDDs: defrag consolidates fragmented files so the read head travels less — improves performance. SSDs: NEVER manually defrag — TRIM handles optimization and defragging causes unnecessary write cycles reducing lifespan. Windows auto-schedules correctly

nodes.title: Troubleshooting: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Troubleshooting. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A Windows PC won't boot and shows 'Operating system not found'. What is the most?
flashcards.back: This error means the BIOS/UEFI cannot find a bootable OS. Check boot order (BIOS), check if SSD/HDD is detected, and run startup repair or bootrec /fixmbr from Windows installation media.

flashcards.front: A user reports their PC is very slow. Task Manager shows 100% disk usage. What i?
flashcards.back: 100% disk usage can be caused by Windows Update, antivirus scan, Search indexing, or a failing hard drive. Check running processes in Task Manager and run CHKDSK to check disk health.

flashcards.front: A PC beeps 3 times and fails to POST. What does this typically indicate?
flashcards.back: Beep codes vary by BIOS vendor. Three beeps often indicate a RAM issue (Award/AMI BIOS). Check that RAM is fully seated, try one stick at a time, or try different slots.

flashcards.front: A PC powers on but nothing appears on the monitor. What are the first three thin?
flashcards.back: Systematic troubleshooting: verify monitor works (try different input/cable), check GPU is properly seated (reseat if needed), listen for POST beep codes indicating RAM/GPU failure. Eliminate simple causes first.

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is virtualization, and what resource allows it on modern CPUs?
flashcards.back: Virtualization lets one physical host run multiple guest OSes simultaneously via a hypervisor (VMware, Hyper-V, VirtualBox). Requires hardware virtualization (VT-x/AMD-V) enabled in BIOS/UEFI for best performance.

flashcards.front: What is Windows Hyper-V?
flashcards.back: Hyper-V is a Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor built into Windows Pro/Enterprise/Server. Requires CPU virtualization (VT-x/AMD-V + SLAT). Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 (WSL2) and Windows Sandbox also use Hyper-V.

flashcards.front: What is virtualization software and name common examples?
flashcards.back: Type 1 hypervisors (bare-metal): VMware ESXi, Hyper-V, Proxmox — run directly on hardware. Type 2 (hosted): VMware Workstation, VirtualBox — run as an application on top of a host OS. Requires VT-x/AMD-V enabled in BIOS.

flashcards.front: What does APIPA stand for and what address range does it use?
flashcards.back: APIPA (169.254.0.1-169.254.255.254) is automatically assigned when a Windows device cannot reach a DHCP server. Seeing a 169.254.x.x address means DHCP has failed — check cable, DHCP server, or scope exhaustion. assigns 169.254.x.x/16 when DHCP is unavailable

pairs.stem: What is the function of DNS in everyday computing?
pairs.option: Translates human-readable domain names (www.google.com) to IP addresses — without DNS, you'd need to memorize IP addresses for every website. Operates hierarchically: root → TLD (.com/.net) → authoritative DNS

pairs.stem: What is the difference between a virus and a worm?
pairs.option: Virus: requires a host file and human action to spread. Worm: self-replicates and spreads automatically over networks without human interaction (exploits vulnerabilities)
